_derivation: 180 s is DERIVED, not chosen -- and the derivation's SCOPE is declared with it rather than overclaimed. The park-time coherence check (ne.runtime.middleware._require_honourable_approval_window) parks only when window <= the caller's remaining authorization, so the largest configurable window is the smallest remaining-at-park this deployment can still hold. Every input is read from its ENFORCEMENT site, not from an observed sample: (1) the console renews the run credential whenever the access token has less than RUN_CREDENTIAL_MIN_REMAINING_SECONDS = 420 s left (packages/ne-console/src/api/client.ts); (2) the enforced per-attempt wall clock is 230 s -- the LARGEST max_steps x _SECONDS_PER_STEP among the agents that can actually park a tier-2 decision, i.e. every agent in deploy/agents/registry.toml whose tool_grants contain an action tiers.rego classifies at tier 2 or higher. Two agents qualify today and they TIE at the maximum: agt_01k3customersupport000000000 (write.external.email.send) and agt_01k3inertparkselftest0000000 (write.external.demo.send), both max_steps = 23 times _SECONDS_PER_STEP = 10 (packages/ne-api/src/ne/api/agent_execution_caps.py), hard-cancelled in ne.runtime.runner.run_model_planned_agent. The SET is derived from the grants, not a named agent id, so moving a tier-2 write onto a longer-budgeted agent re-derives this number instead of silently invalidating it; (3) OIDC verification budgets leeway_seconds = 10 s of clock skew (packages/ne-identity/src/ne/identity/config.py). 420 - 230 - 10 = 180. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is NOT a worst-case bound, and it is not claimed as one. RUN_CREDENTIAL_MIN_REMAINING_SECONDS is a FAIL-OPEN RENEW TRIGGER, not a floor -- the console returns early when no renew hook is installed and swallows a failed renew ('Fail-open to the current token'), and it binds the console alone, so a run started from the API or the CLI has no such trigger at all. 180 s is therefore THE LARGEST WINDOW THAT HOLDS WHEN THE CONSOLE'S RENEW SUCCEEDS. DECLARED RESIDUALS, all five: (a) a run admitted on a fail-open renew, or started outside the console, can still refuse at park; (b) THE WINDOW RESERVES NOTHING FOR THE RESUMED ATTEMPT -- 230 s is ONE attempt's cap, the pre-park stretch, and the resume runs the same cap again, so at the maximum park time the resumed attempt starts with essentially none of the caller's authorization left and the delayed-seam guard refuses it (reserving a second 230 s would make 420 - 230 - 230 - 10 negative, i.e. no honourable window at all on this deployment). 180 s is the largest window that can be PARKED honourably; it does not guarantee the park RESUMES. A decision landing in the final moments also races the resume seam, because the guard refuses at now >= expires_at and the resume happens after the decision; (c) dispatch latency -- admission, enqueue, worker pickup between the console's freshness check and the attempt's first step -- is an OMITTED term, unbounded, though measured pre-loop work is ~0.11 s so it errs safe today; (d) leeway_seconds is a CLASS DEFAULT, overridable by NE_IDENTITY_OIDC__LEEWAY_SECONDS anywhere in 0-60; nothing under deploy/ sets it, and the window test asserts that rather than assuming it; (e) THIS VALUE IS STILL INTERIM AND F1 HAS NOW LANDED WITHOUT MOVING IT -- the standing approval survives the owner's token, so on a tier-2/3 park -- where tiers.rego resolves a non-NULL standing lifetime, floors 7 d and 2 d -- a decision taken past the horizon is written as a standing approval in the same transaction that terminalizes the attempt, and the owner's next authenticated run re-parks, re-checks every stamp live and consumes it. That changes what this ceiling COSTS rather than the ceiling itself. Every input above is unchanged, _require_honourable_approval_window still refuses a DECLARED window longer than the owner's remaining authorization, and this document still declares 180. Raising the number needs one of those inputs to move, and F1 moved none of them; nor does F1's rescue reach the workflow write legs described below, which park with a NULL standing lifetime and therefore mint nothing. SCOPED TO THE ACTION, NOT THE TIER, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The derivation is about ONE thing: the pre-park stretch of a Run executed by an agent that holds a tier-2 write grant. Declaring it under approval_windows.tiers would apply it to every tier-2/3 approval on every path -- including the conversation park (DurableApprovalGate.request_approval), which has no durable resume seam for the horizon to collide with (ne.api.workflows dispatches its _park as a background asyncio.create_task, so the request returns while it polls, and nothing re-binds the owner's admitted context afterwards) -- silently cutting those approvals from the 4 h/24 h floor to three minutes for a reason that says nothing about them. So it is declared under approval_windows.actions for write.external.email.send. Every other action keeps tiers.rego's built-in floor, exactly as before. GRANTING A NEW TIER-2 ACTION TO AN AGENT SHOULD BE ACCOMPANIED BY DECLARING ITS WINDOW HERE: until then the built-in floor applies, and the park-time coherence check does NOT refuse it -- it warns and parks, because refusing on a floor punishes a decision nobody took -- so the cost of forgetting is a silent four-hour promise, not a loud failure. ⭐ NE-ITEM1-INERT-PARK: write.external.email.send IS NO LONGER THE ONLY TIER-2 GRANT, and the second one is DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDECLARED. agt_01k3inertparkselftest0000000 (Governance Self-Test) holds write.external.demo.send -- an action whose handler performs no I/O at all (ne.api.demo_seams._demo_writeback_handler returns a constant string) -- so that POST_DEMO item 1 ("parked runs can never terminalize") can be exercised on this deployment with zero outward effect. Declaring a window for it would DEFEAT that: a declared 180 s makes the durable row expire as an ORDINARY approval timeout and the run reconciles EXPIRED, which is exactly the reason PR #938's clamp was reverted -- the specific authorization_expired terminalization, and the whole path item 1 names, would never run. Its park is meant to outlive the owner's horizon on the built-in floor, so a self-test left unanswered dies the way the production defect died. It does not move the 230 s ceiling either, and NE-INERT-BUDGET (registry generation 25 / agent version 2) is what makes that a deliberate statement rather than an accident: its max_steps was raised 6 -> 23 because at 6 the enforced turn wall clock is 60 s, and the ONE governed read.knowledge.search its park requires -- middleware._run_source_references refuses a Tier-2 park with no server-observed evidence -- costs 108-207 s on this deployment, whose reranker runs BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 on 12 CPUs with no GPU. At 6 it could not park at all: three live attempts, zero parks. 23 is the CEILING this very derivation sets, so the two parking agents now TIE there, the subtrahend is still 230 and this document still declares 180. Raising it to 24 would drop the ceiling to 170 and refuse every write.external.email.send park, so the residual -- the slowest observed read plus warm overhead is about 231 s and STILL overruns 230 -- belongs to the reranker and cannot be bought off in the registry. Do not add it to the actions map. ⛔ AND DECLARING WINDOWS HERE CANNOT COVER EVERY PARK. The workflow write legs (write.internal.crm.note under write_approval_floor_scope(TIER_2)) reach the guard with NO policy window at all: the ToolSpec declares tier 1, the PDP is asked about tier 1 and answers allow with a null window, and the tier-2 floor is applied afterwards by _effective_tier, which the PDP never sees. No entry in this document can intercept a chain that never consults it. ⚠️ AND SEE RESIDUAL (e): this value guarantees an honourable PARK, not a completing RESUME -- at maximum park time the resumed attempt has about 10 s of horizon left. It is what this deployment can honour - it is NOT a recommendation and NOT the 4 h the tier-2 floor promises. See docs/architecture/approval-horizon.md.
